short: Si substituted hydroxyapatite nanorods on Ti for percutaneou
title: Si substituted hydroxyapatite nanorods on Ti for percutaneous implants

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: Percutaneous implants need a tight skin seal; bare Ti lets epithelium grow down along the implant and a fibrous capsule form. Si-substituted hydroxyapatite nanorods on Ti should enhance fibroblast function and skin integration.
states.detail: Absorbed: n1 (HYP/need), n2 (HYP/hypothesis), n3 (DES/base_system), n4 (DES/modification), n6 (PRC/deposition)

states.title: Structure state
states.head: Both coatings are arrays of hexagonal nanorods growing from the Ti; Si does not change the rod morphology. Si is incorporated in the Si-HA nanorods at about 3-5% and is absent from HA.
states.detail: Absorbed: n7 (STR/microstructure/shape), n9 (STR/chemistry/composition), n10 (STR/phase/site_occupancy), n11 (STR/phase/lattice). Premises: Si 2p at ~101.8 eV = orthosilicate SiO4 4- on phosphate sites; ~103.1 eV = three-dimensional silicate

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: Si-HA releases more Ca than HA at every immersion time and also releases Si (~0.5-0.6 ppm by 28 d). Fibroblast adhesion at 1 d ranks Si-HA > HA > Ti.
states.detail: Absorbed: n12 (PRP/value), n14 (PRP/value), n16 (PRP/value), n17 (PRP/value), n18 (MEC/pathway), n19 (MEC/pathway). Premises: Silicate-for-phosphate substitution distorts the apatite lattice and raises its solubility; Si and Ca ions from bioactive ceramics stimulate fibroblast proliferation and collagen/ECM gene expression; In fibroblasts TGF-b1 and CTGF drive alpha-SMA and Col-I expression and collagen deposition

states.title: Performance state
states.head: After 4 weeks in vivo Si-HA pillars show little epithelial down-growth and no fibrous capsule; HA partly, Ti poorly integrated with skin

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: Si-substituted HA nanorod coatings on Ti enhance fibroblast adhesion, fibrogenic function and skin sealing, making them promising for percutaneous implants

nodes.title: MICRO, F1
nodes.head: Top views show densely packed rods with hexagonal ends in both coatings; no visible difference in rod shape
nodes.solves: Both coatings are arrays of hexagonal nanorods growing from the Ti; Si does not change the rod morphology
nodes.note: 10 um insets: uniform coverage in both
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n7 (o1).

nodes.title: EDS:spectrum, TEM, XPS:region, F1, F3, F4
nodes.head: Surface EDS of the Si-HA coating reads Si 3.11 wt%. EDS points along a Si-HA cross-section read Si 3.93, 3.79, 3.88, 3.19, 2.15 wt% from top to bottom.
nodes.solves: Si is incorporated in the Si-HA nanorods at about 3-5% and is absent from HA
nodes.op: compare across conditions, read characteristic point, register colocated views
nodes.note: Ca also drops 18.5 to 14.2 at%, so Ca/P 1.48 to 1.37
nodes.detail: o7: Surface EDS of the Si-HA coating reads Si 3.11 wt%; o8: EDS points along a Si-HA cross-section read Si 3.93, 3.79, 3.88, 3.19, 2.15 wt% from top to bottom; o9: TEM-EDS: a Si peak near 1.74 keV appears only for the Si-HA rod; Ca, P, O in both, Cu from grid; o10: XPS survey: Si 2p/2s peaks only on Si-HA; inset table Si 4.9 at% (Si-HA) vs 0 (HA), P 10.4 vs 12.5 at%

nodes.title: evidence, F4
nodes.head: Asymmetric Si 2p envelope fitted with two components at 101.8 eV and 103.1 eV. The 103.1 eV (non-lattice silicate) component carries roughly a third of the Si 2p area, the 101.8 eV component about two thirds
nodes.solves: Si sits on phosphate sites as orthosilicate SiO4 4- replacing PO4 3- in the HA lattice
nodes.note: peak heights ~0.62 vs ~0.37 of envelope with similar widths; text assigns both but never states the split
nodes.detail: o11: Asymmetric Si 2p envelope fitted with two components at 101.8 eV and 103.1 eV; o12: The 103.1 eV (non-lattice silicate) component carries roughly a third of the Si 2p area, the 101.8 eV component about two thirds

nodes.title: MICRO, F7
nodes.head: Actin/nucleus images at 1 d: few round cells on Ti (~9 per field), more on HA (~17) and most, more spread, on Si-HA (~22)
nodes.solves: Fibroblast adhesion at 1 d ranks Si-HA > HA > Ti
nodes.note: spreading differences are modest; counts are rough per-field estimates
nodes.necessity_reason: No member reaches image_support shown, and n14 keeps shown support from o18.

nodes.title: evidence, F5
nodes.head: Accumulated Ca from Si-HA exceeds Ca from HA at every time (2.5 vs 1.5 ppm at 28 d); Si from Si-HA rises to ~0.6 ppm
nodes.solves: Si-HA releases more Ca than HA at every immersion time and also releases Si (~0.5-0.6 ppm by 28 d)
nodes.note: text gives Si ~0.5 ppm at 28 d; plot ~0.6. Si curve flat from 3 to 14 d. Ca fast within 14 d then slower, Si-HA still rising 2.2 to 2.5
nodes.detail: o16: Accumulated Ca from Si-HA exceeds Ca from HA at every time (2.5 vs 1.5 ppm at 28 d); Si from Si-HA rises to ~0.6 ppm
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n12 (o16).

nodes.title: evidence, F6
nodes.head: Adsorbed protein: HA ~30/40 and Si-HA ~29/40 ug/mL vs Ti ~15/19 at 4/24 h
nodes.solves: Nanorod topography raises protein adsorption, which with Si substitution promotes initial fibroblast attachment and spreading
nodes.detail: o17: Adsorbed protein: HA ~30/40 and Si-HA ~29/40 ug/mL vs Ti ~15/19 at 4/24 h
nodes.necessity_reason: Only figure-backed support with image_support shown for n19 (o17).

nodes.title: evidence, F8
nodes.head: At 7 d all four genes rank Si-HA > HA > Ti (e.g. TGF-b1 2.14 > 1.86 > 1.52).
nodes.solves: Si-HA up-regulates fibrogenic genes (TGF-b1, CTGF, alpha-SMA, Col-I) in fibroblasts above HA and Ti
